steps.title: Collect and Prepare Fungal Sample
steps.instruction: Collect mycelia from culture media in a Petri-dish or extract internal tissue from a fresh fruiting mushroom body (stalk or cap) using a sterile scalpel or scissors.

steps.title: Rinse and Squeeze Mycelia
steps.instruction: If using mycelia, rinse the sample with approximately 3 ml of autoclaved ultrapure water using sterile medical pads and manually squeeze. The sample should be thawed at room temperature for a maximum of 90 min before use. Biomass can be rinsed by adding 1 ml of water separately using a P1000 while spreading it over the surface.

steps.title: Freeze and Pulverize Sample
steps.instruction: Prepare the sample as a fine powder and store at low temperatures.

substeps.instruction: Place the collected tissue or rinsed/squeezed mycelia at -20°C for 48h.
Pulverize the sample into a fine powder using liquid nitrogen treatment with a porcelain mortar and pestle in a cold environment.
Place the resulting fine powder immediately at -20°C for 12-24h.
Alternatively, freeze-dry the frozen mushroom sample for 1 cycle of 24h.
Store the fine powder at -20°C or -80°C until use.

steps.title: Initial Lysis
steps.instruction: Place 100-300 mg of the fine powder into a QIAGEN DNeasy Plant Pro Kit tissue disruption tube at -20°C for 48h, then add lysis solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µl of Solution CD1 to the tube. (Note: If the sample is high in phenolic compounds, use 450 µl Solution CD1 and 50 µl Solution PS).
Vortex to initially mix and disrupt the sample.
Seal the tube lid with Parafilm and vortex at maximum speed for 5–20 min (average 15 min). For samples ≤100 mg, vortex for 3–10 min, or 10–15 min depending on the fungi aspect (mushroom vs mycelia).

steps.title: First Centrifugation and Supernatant Recovery
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tissue disruption tubes at 12,000 g for 2 min at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Transfer exactly 400 µl of the supernatant to a new, clean, autoclaved 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Optional: Store the used disruption tube and pellet at -20°C for up to 3 days for further extraction.

steps.title: Secondary Lysis and Precipitation
steps.instruction: Add cold Solution CD2 to the recovered supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µl of cold Solution CD2 (4°C) and vortex for 5 s.
Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 1 min at room temperature.
Carefully transfer exactly 450 µl of the upper portion of the supernatant to a new, clean, autoclaved 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube, avoiding the pellet.

steps.title: Binding and Column Loading
steps.instruction: Prepare the lysate for the MB Spin Column.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µl of Buffer APP to the supernatant and vortex for 5 s.
Load 600 µl of the resulting lysate onto an MB Spin Column.
Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 1 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash with Buffer AW1
steps.instruction: Wash the bound DNA using Buffer AW1.

substeps.instruction: Add 650 µl of Buffer AW1 to the MB spin column.
Place the column into a new, clean, autoclaved 2 ml collection tube.
Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 1 min to pass the lysate through the column.
Discard the flow-through.
Add any remaining lysate volume to the column and repeat the centrifugation at 12,000 g for 1 min.
Centrifuge again at 12,000 g for 1 min, then centrifuge at 15,000 g for 4 min to ensure all volume has passed through.

steps.title: Wash with Buffer AW2
steps.instruction: Perform the final wash and dry the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Discard the flow-through, tap the tube on hygienic paper to remove excess liquid, and return the column to the 2 ml collection tube.
Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 1 min.
Add 650 µl of Buffer AW2 to the MB spin column.
Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 1 min to pass the Buffer AW1/AW2 volume through the column.
Discard the flow-through, tap the tube on hygienic paper, and return the column to the 2 ml collection tube.
Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 1 min.

steps.title: DNA Elution
steps.instruction: Elute the gDNA from the column membrane.

substeps.instruction: Place the MB spin column into a new, clean, autoclaved 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube (cut the tube cap before centrifuging if processing multiple tubes).
Add Buffer EB to the center of the white filter membrane based on the intended application:
General: 15-50 µl
Illumina: 30-60 µl
Nanopore (ONT): 10-20 µl
Optimum yield: 15-30 µl (mycelia) or 10-20 µl (mushroom).
Incubate for 1-2 min.
Centrifuge at 13,000 g for 2 min at room temperature.
Transfer the obtained volume into a new, clean, autoclaved 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Quality Control
steps.instruction: Verify the quantity and integrity of the extracted gDNA.

substeps.instruction: Quantify and check quality using a Fragment Analyser (especially for ONT to ensure a unimodal distribution with fragments ≥10Kb).
Perform Gel Electrophoresis: 2% Agarose Gel, 1x Tris Borate EDTA (TBE) buffer, run for 1h at 100V with a 1Kb size estimator.
